plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on prior iteration observations. Previous 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 designs showed thickness excursions beyond 1200 nm (iterations 01, 09, 13), which complicates deposition control and increases stress. Feedback directive specifies constraining thickness search to 700-1100 nm with optical-path difference penalty to enforce smoother phase progression. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 with refined bounds and smoothness penalty, (2) 22-layer Ge/Nb2O5 alternative material pair validated for methane sensing at 3300 nm, (3) 18-layer ZnS/MgF2 reduced count to test manufacturability-performance tradeoff within evidence-based thickness constraints.

routes.title: 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 with Bounded Thickness and Optical-Path Smoothness Penalty
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining layer thicknesses to 700-1100 nm range while penalizing optical-path differences between adjacent layers will suppress the 1200+ nm excursions observed in prior iterations, yielding smoother phase progression across the stack while maintaining dual-band transmittance performance for CH4 and CO2 sensing bands.
routes.design_principle: Alternating high-low index quarter-wave stack with thickness bounds informed by prior iteration deviations. Optical-path smoothness penalty enforces gradual phase accumulation rather than abrupt thickness jumps that complicate deposition control.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | CaF2 substrate. Total 22 finite layers.

routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate under air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2 (22 finite layers total). All layer thicknesses bounded to [700, 1100] nm. Optimize for high mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm passbands, low mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm stopbands. Include optical-path difference penalty in loss function to suppress thickness excursions and enforce smooth phase progression. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with coherent TMM solver. Normal unpolarized illumination. No metal layers. Evaluate all 22 thicknesses as continuous design variables. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Refines route_01 based on feedback directive to constrain thickness search to 700-1100 nm and introduce optical-path difference penalty. Prior iterations showed thickness excursions beyond 1200 nm (iteration 01: 1601 nm, 1865 nm; iteration 09: 1575 nm, 1506 nm; iteration 13: 1249 nm). This revision directly addresses those deviations while preserving the 22-layer topology that achieved highest target score (0.955) in iteration 01.

routes.title: 22-Layer Ge/Nb2O5 Dual-Band Filter Validated for Methane Sensing
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Ge/Nb2O5 material pair, evidenced for methane sensor bandpass filters at 3300 nm center wavelength, will achieve comparable or improved dual-band performance versus ZnS/MgF2 while offering different dispersion characteristics that may better separate the CH4 and CO2 bands.
routes.design_principle: Literature-evidenced Ge/Nb2O5 multilayer design for methane sensing at 3300 nm (CorpusId:139773493). Alternating high-low index stack with thicknesses optimized for dual-band transmission at 3.3 μm and 4.25 μm.

routes.title: 18-Layer ZnS/MgF2 with Tighter Thickness Bounds for Manufacturability
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 22 to 18 while maintaining 700-1100 nm thickness bounds will preserve adequate dual-band performance while improving manufacturability through reduced deposition time and stress accumulation, based on evidence that coating thickness directly impacts vacuum chamber residence time and quality control difficulty.
routes.design_principle: Thickness-constrained design per CorpusId:17683472 evidence limiting infrared coatings to ~40 μm total thickness. 18 layers at ~900 nm average yields ~16 μm total, well within manufacturability limits while preserving sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization.
